name: Investor Residence (Investment Encouragement Act)

requirements.blocker_text: Earnest money deposit of at least US$250,000 (or foreign-currency equivalent acceptable to the Central Bank), transferred externally, required before an investment license is issued.
requirements.fix_path: Transfer at least US$250,000 in earnest money via an external bank transfer acceptable to Sudan's Central Bank.

evidence_required.document: Proof of external bank transfer of earnest money

outcome.duration_length: residence granted for the duration of the investment project, subject to applicable immigration laws and regulations not yet issued at the time of this build

sources.title: UNCTAD Investment Policy Hub -- Sudan's Investment (Encouragement) Act, 2021: Section 22 requires foreign investors to deposit at least US$250,000 earnest money via external transfer before a license is issued; Section 21 grants non-Sudanese investors residence for the duration of their project, 'without violation to the provisions of the laws organizing the same and as the regulations may specify' -- i.e. subject to separate immigration regulations

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sudan). STATUS: DRAFT -- the only source located for this Act's operative text is UNCTAD's Investment Policy Hub, tier-2 (intergovernmental) under this dataset's convention; Sudan's own Ministry of Investment portal (sudaninvest.org) was confirmed to exist and be reachable in this build, but its specific investment-threshold and residence-rights pages were not independently retrieved -- worth a direct follow-up attempt there before treating this as the final word. STRUCTURAL FINDING: the Act's own text explicitly defers the actual residence mechanics to separate regulations described as not yet fully specified at the time of the Act's text -- meaning even a tier-1 confirmation of the Act itself would likely still leave the practical work/residence rights underspecified. family_can_join is set to false as a conservative schema-compliant default (the field does not accept null) rather than an invented affirmative right -- nothing in the source addresses dependents at all, so this should not be read as a confirmed exclusion, only as the absence of a confirmed inclusion. GIVEN THE POLITICAL AND SECURITY CONTEXT DISCLOSED IN sd_entry_visa.json -- an active civil war, a capital only recently reoccupied by the government, and large-scale destruction of infrastructure -- the practical viability of a genuine USD 250,000 foreign direct investment in Sudan as of this build's date is a materially separate question from whether the legal mechanism exists on paper; this dataset models the latter only.
